What JavaScript Is:
The seven primitive types and the one structural type, checked at run time:

```js
console.log(
  typeof 1,          // 'number'
  typeof 1n,         // 'bigint'
  typeof 'a',        // 'string'
  typeof true,       // 'boolean'
  typeof undefined,  // 'undefined'
  typeof Symbol(),   // 'symbol'
  typeof null,       // 'object'  <- the famous historical bug
  typeof {},         // 'object'
  typeof (() => {}), // 'function'
);
```

The single number type is a 64-bit float, which is why the classic decimal case fails:

```js
console.log(0.1 + 0.2);              // 0.30000000000000004
console.log(0.1 + 0.2 === 0.3);      // false
console.log(Math.abs(0.1 + 0.2 - 0.3) < Number.EPSILON);  // true
```

And the three special numbers that are not errors:

```js
console.log(1 / 0, -1 / 0, 0 / 0);   // Infinity -Infinity NaN
console.log(NaN === NaN);            // false — NaN is not equal to itself
console.log(Object.is(NaN, NaN));    // true
```
